walkthroughs.body_html:
Applied Methods of Sociological Enquiry — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Applied Methods of Sociological Enquiry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Applied Methods of Sociological Enquiry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Weber's concept for empathetic understanding of social action is:
options: Anomie
Verstehen
Praxis
Alienation

mcqs.q: Which research method involves in-depth participant observation?
options: Survey
Experiment
Ethnography
Content analysis

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary data?
options: Primary data means the first page of a report.
Primary data is collected first-hand by the researcher; secondary data already exists and was produced by others.
Drawing triangles to display data.
Primary data is always more valuable than secondary data.

mcqs.q: Why do positivists prefer quantitative methods?
options: Because numbers are simply easier to collect than words.
Because they reject all forms of observation.
Because they seek objective, measurable patterns and law-like generalisations about society.
Drawing triangles to display data.

mcqs.q: What is triangulation in social research?
options: Because they reject all forms of observation.
Always using exactly three different researchers.
Using more than one method or source to check and strengthen findings.
Drawing triangles to display data.
